skills.name: Hear and tell apart words with bl, sp, sc, sk and ck
skills.mastery: The child hears and picks out words with bl, sp, sc, sk and ck (sc and sk both say /sk/) in a sentence or conversation (for example black, spoon, school, desk, duck) and tells them from words that differ by one sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: circle the words with the sound

skills.name: Know and choose the new words of the theme
skills.mastery: The child chooses the theme word that fits a sentence or picture (for example duster, sweep, matatu, July, shopkeeper, seedling, bandage, chalkboard, calf, left, litter, radio, dance, chores, sick) and does not swap it for a word of the same group. sub_strands.sub_strand: Verb ‘to be’- Past Tense Objective Pronouns - Plural (Theme 1: School)
learning_experiences: work with peers to pick out the plural forms of the objective pronouns (us, you and them) and the past forms of the verb ‘to be’ (was and were) from a text,
listen to a story, poem, or conversation from an audio recording/ teacher model featuring the past forms of the verb ‘to be’ (was and were),
pick out sentences showing the past forms of the verb ‘to be’ (was and were),
form sentences with was and were,
form sentences with the plural forms of the objective pronouns (us, you and them) from substitution tables,
work in groups to write the plural forms of the objective pronouns (us, you and them) on a poster or chart and display it,
practise the use of was and were during role-play, language games or songs.
key_inquiry_questions: How do we talk about an action in the past?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity and imagination: This is enhanced as the learner builds on their creativity skills when writing the plural forms of the objective pronouns (us, you and them) on a poster or chart and display it.
Collaboration: Teamwork is reinforced as the learner collaborates with others in role-play activities and language games observing the rules of engagement.
sub_strands.values: Respect: Patience is nurtured as the learner gives others equal opportunities to pick out the plural forms of the objective pronouns (us, you and them) and the past forms of the verb ‘to be’ (was and were) from a text.
sub_strands.pcis: Life Skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is reinforced as they communicate effectively using correct forms of tense and language.
sub_strands.links: The learner can apply the knowledge of the past forms of the verb ‘to be’ to learning of similar concepts in Kiswahili Language Activities.

misconceptions.cause: Full stops are used for all.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "." beside "?" in a fresh sentence or text and ask again; picking it again shows the error is still there.
misconceptions.source: to confirm by a Kenyan English teacher: a common classroom error of Kenyan learners of English, written offline (18 Nov 2026), not traced to a study

misconceptions.error: Forgets the capital after a full stop.

example.question: Correct: We helped. we cared.

misconceptions.cause: Only the first sentence gets a capital.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "We helped. we cared." beside "We helped. We cared." in a fresh sentence or text and ask again; picking it again shows the error is still there.
